description: Usage rules in the decision profile v1alpha1 (docs/contracts/module-contract-v0.1.md, section 6.11), with the file's catalog, whose argument declarations give each argument its type. generator: each case is a policy of the scope given, global or agent, with its usage rules, an array given as a JSON value in rules or as text in rules_text, where a parsed value cannot hold it; statements is the text that the generator writes, null when it refuses a rule. The text is compared once parsed, as the check of generated text compares statements; the Go and Python stacks also write it exactly, in the layout of section 6.11's example, with an empty line between statements. The rule's JSON is I-JSON apart from the size of its integers, and no string of the rule holds a control character (the review of 2026-11-16). checks: each case is a policy's text of the scope given, and accepted says whether the core's check accepts it when the version is submitted: each statement that carries @rule, regenerated from its annotation, equals once parsed what the generator writes, and every rule is whole, its statements exactly those the generator writes, none missing, none added and none repeated. cases: calls decided as catalog-check.json decides them, whose description says how, with the policies of each case, among them policies of usage rules that the generator wrote, and hand-written statements whose annotations read as a rule or not. A policy.forbid decision names in rules each distinct pair of policy ID and rule ID among the forbidding statements whose annotation reads as a rule, sorted by code point, policy ID first, then rule ID; rules is absent when it names none. An annotation reads as a rule when it is the JSON of an object with exactly description, id, tool and when, each read as the generator reads it, without the catalog or the policy's scope (the review of 2026-11-16).
